title: Search underway for incarcerated woman who walked away from San Diego Female Community Reentry Program - NewsBreak
text:
By Domenick Candelieri California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation ,
1 days ago
SAN DIEGO (FOX 5/KUSI) — An incarcerated woman in a Female Community Reentry Program (FCRP) in San Diego County walked away from the facility Tuesday.
Angel Rayburn, 37, was confirmed missing around 9:05 p.m. after security officials were alerted that she had tampered with her ankle monitor and walked out of the FCRP facility, the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation said on its website.
Rayburn was last seen wearing black sweatpants, black sweatshirt and white sneakers near the intersection of Kearny Mesa Road and Armstrong Street in San Diego. She is described as 5 feet, 5 inches tall and weighing around 155 pounds with brown hair and brown eyes.
Lawsuit filed over unsanitary conditions at San Diego safe sleeping sites On Feb. 14, Rayburn, who has been housed at FCRP San Diego since Aug. 14, was originally received from Riverside to serve a three-year sentence for evading a peace officer while driving the wrong way, assault with any means likely to produce GBI to peace officer/firefighter and buy/receive stolen vehicle/trailer/construction equipment, according to CDCR officials.
Anyone who sees Rayburn or knows about her whereabouts should contact law enforcement, call 911 or contact Special Agent Guillermo Lopez at 619-666-5523.
